## An Argument Value That Starts No Expression [error]

A missing separator and a value that is not a value are different mistakes.
Nothing is missing between `(` and `*` here, so the diagnostic is about the
expression rather than about a comma, and the tokens up to the next boundary go
into the value slot of the argument that wanted them.

```r
fn(* 1)
fn(a, * 1)
fn(a = * 1)
fn(,, * 1)
```

## Closing Delimiter Belonging To Someone Else [error]

The argument list ends at any closing delimiter, not just its own, so the `}`
survives for its owner rather than being eaten as an argument. Nothing was
written between the `(` and the `}`, so the list is empty rather than holding
one empty argument.

```r
fn(}
```

```cst
RRoot {
    bom_token: missing (optional),
    statements: RStatementList [
        RStatement {
            expression: RCall {
                function: RIdentifier {
                    name_token: IDENT@0..2 "fn" [] [],
                },
                arguments: RCallArguments {
                    l_paren_token: L_PAREN@2..3 "(" [] [],
                    items: RArgumentList [],
                    r_paren_token: missing (required),
                },
            },
            semicolon_token: missing (optional),
        },
        RStatement {
            expression: RBogusExpression {
                items: [
                    R_CURLY@3..4 "}" [] [],
                ],
            },
            semicolon_token: missing (optional),
        },
    ],
    eof_token: EOF@4..5 "" [Newline("\n")] [],
}
```

## A Newline Or Comment Between A Name And Its `=`

`parse_argument()` looks one token past the name to find the `=`, and that
lookahead skips trivia to reach it

```r
f(a
  = 1)

f(a # c
  = 1)

f("a" # c
  = 1)
```
